title: close notifications hotkey and/or dbus command (close / clear / remove)
line: A new "Hide Notification Popups" global shortcut hides every notification popup on screen at once, keeping them in the history.
explanation: The notifications applet only had global shortcuts for Do Not Disturb and for clearing the history, so popups that never time out (or critical ones) had to be closed one by one, and there was no D-Bus call for it either. The applet now registers a "Hide Notification Popups" global shortcut (plasmashell component, no default key). It hides every popup on screen the same way its own timeout would: notifications move to the history and running jobs are dismissed into the applet, where they keep going. Like any global shortcut it can also be called over D-Bus: qdbus6 org.kde.kglobalaccel /component/plasmashell invokeShortcut "hide popups".

commits.message:
applets/notifications: add a global shortcut to hide notification popups

Popups that never time out could only be removed by closing each one. A
new "Hide Notification Popups" global shortcut hides them all as if they
had timed out, so they stay in the history and running jobs go on.

BUG: 500308

media.caption: Master: three popups that never time out plus a running copy job stay on screen; the only notification shortcuts are Toggle Do Not Disturb and Clear Notification History
With the fix: the same popups and job, then the Hide Notification Popups shortcut is triggered and all of them disappear at once
Master: the popups can only be removed by closing each one
After hiding: the notifications are still in the history and the copy job keeps running in the applet
